results.content: The August data extends a turbulent stretch for consumer confidence that began when conflict in the Middle East disrupted oil markets and drove up gasoline prices. Sentiment rebounded in June from a record low set in May, when the index fell to 44.8 amid surging pump prices and deepening concern that inflation would spread beyond fuel costs. The June recovery was driven in part by falling gasoline prices, though consumers remained worried about the cost of living.
